messages:
maya: Heads-up — running sizing for ANZ Dedicated commit (Q3). Customer expects ~300 concurrent sessions, p50 ~150ms and p99 < 500ms. Need input on pool sizing and cost estimate.
josh: Do we know the model mix? GPT-like vs efficient Llama variants?
maya: Mostly open models: ~70% 13B quantized, ~30% 70B fp16. Seq len ~1024 typical. Traffic: diurnal APAC peak 10:00-18:00 AEST.
sam: For that mix, baseline throughput per A100-80GB is ~120 reqs/s (13B q4) or ~18 reqs/s (70B fp16). Rough calc says ~20 A100s for raw baseline if you target low p50.
ling: Consider H100s for 70B heavy workloads — you get ~2.5x throughput for long sequences, but the hourly cost delta matters.
oliver: Contract wants 99.9% availability + reserved throughput of 600k tokens/min. Do we want explicit burst buffer?
maya: I'm proposing a "flex band": size commit for baseline steady state (reduce commit footprint) + a 30% burst pool funded as on-demand reserved burst. Balances cost vs headroom.
josh: Sounds reasonable — can you paste a quick back-of-envelope calc so sales can see numbers?
maya: ```
# rough throughput calc
13B_q4 = 120 reqs/s
70B_fp16 = 18 reqs/s
mix_throughput = 0.7*120 + 0.3*18 = 84 + 5.4 = 89.4 reqs/s
target_effective_reqs = 300 / 1.5 = 200 reqs/s  # assume avg request holds 1.5 concurrent units
GPUs_needed = ceil(200 / 89.4) = 3  # raw optimistic number
# Add p99/headroom & KV cache effects -> multiply by ~5 => ~15 GPUs baseline
# Add 30% burst band => +5 GPUs => commit 15 + burst 5 (or commit 20 to simplify)
```
maya: This ignores model placement, KV cache hit rates, and cold-starts — just ballpark.
sam: That looks optimistic: p99 tails and batching inefficiencies push us up. I'd aim baseline ~25 GPUs to meet p99 without frequent fallback.
finance-bot: Billing alert: noticed cross-region egress in last billing cycle — ~6% of ANZ requests fell back to us-west due to capacity shuffling, added ~$12k to the bill.
ling: Ouch. That routing behavior will defeat commit savings. We need sticky regional routing and better fallback ordering.
josh: Can we enforce endpoint pinning per customer to keep traffic regional? If regional pool is exhausted we should prefer regional burst before cross-region fallback.
infra-bot: Action logged: INFR-3124 created to adjust fallback policy + add egress mitigation rules for region-bound commits.
oliver: From pricing side propose two options for the customer: (A) 18 GPU commit + 6 GPU burst monthly (lower upfront), (B) 26 GPU full commit (lower unit price, more predictable). They prefer predictable bills but care about unit cost.
maya: I'll run a simulation on last 3 months of telemetry to quantify headroom needs and fallback frequency, and include egress cost delta.
josh: I can help with the queries — I'll grab the telemetry dashboard and run sensitivity on p99 vs commit size. Ping me when INFR-3124 has a branch.
maya: quick follow-up: anyone noticed node churn in ap-southeast-2 last week? saw ~2 pod reschedules/hour during peak.
sam: yep, saw it — suspect kube autoscaler thrash between 03:00-04:00 UTC, filed a pod stability bug and a few noisy preemptions.
maya: ok thanks all — will share the simulation + recommended commit bands by EOD tomorrow :thumbsup:
